source.title: PhysSAE: Mechanistic Interpretability of PINNs with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Nandita N. Patil; A. EshwarR; G. Honnavar

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether SAE dictionary atoms recur across random SAE seeds and reports low matched similarity, arguing that the dictionaries are non-unique. This challenges the stable/canonical-units part of V5, but it does not test whether the features are complete.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE-to-concept alignment, hidden-state ablations, comparisons with PCA/ICA, and overcompleteness and sparsity sweeps. These results concern PINN representations and their interpretation, but do not test the superposition geometry in V1, neuron capacity/polysemanticity in V2, polysemanticity without capacity pressure in V3, LLM representations in V4, or dimensionality of superposed features in V6. The cross-seed feature-consistency results bear on V5. Other results are not rows for the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains 3 SAEs with different seeds on each frozen PINN and Hungarian-matches their decoder dictionaries. Matched cosine is about 0.35 and only 1–2% of atoms exceed 0.7. The authors state that SAE dictionaries are non-unique. This directly bears on the 'stable, canonical units' part of V5, in a non-LLM setting (small tanh MLP PINNs). No other version is tested: the alignment, intervention and ablation results concern PINN interpretability, not superposition geometry, capacity, or LLMs.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that PINNs develop sparse, physically structured latent representations. SAE atoms align with independent physical observables and have localized causal effects that beat PCA/ICA and matched controls. They treat the non-uniqueness of SAE dictionaries across seeds as expected for overcomplete sparse coding. They argue it does not undermine their claims, because causal localization is stable across PINN seeds.
record.recipe_differences: Trains overcomplete ReLU SAEs on penultimate-layer activations of frozen PINNs and evaluates their features against independent PDE reference fields; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE atom identity varies across random SAE seeds. The authors report that causal localization is stable across PINN seeds for four of six PDEs, with ESF80 standard deviation below 0.05.

fits_no_version.finding: In PINNs, the top SAE atoms correlate with independently computed physical concept fields. Mean max |r| is 0.675–0.943, with permutation Z above 40. Alignment rises with dictionary size D=128→512 (Tables 3, 5). Alignment matrices show atoms aligned to one or two concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs recover sparse, concept-aligned (monosemantic-like) features in non-language scientific networks such as PINNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept-aligned causal localisation (ESF80) has a standard deviation below 0.05 across PINN seeds on four of six PDEs. This holds even though SAE atoms are not stable across SAE seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional properties of SAE decompositions can be seed-stable even when individual dictionary atoms are not.

record.code_released: not stated; code and checkpoints are promised upon acceptance
record.problems: The study tests only modest 5-layer, width-128 PINNs on 1+1D PDEs. Cross-seed cosine values are reported without uncertainty estimates, and aggregation across PINN seeds for Table 8 is not stated. Its stability test does not establish completeness of SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the relevant cross-seed consistency results in Table 8. Other reported alignment, intervention, ablation, and PINN-quality results were left out because they do not measure the claim versions tested here.

untested.parts: Completeness of SAE features is not tested. Canonicality across dictionary sizes or architectures is not tested. Stability in LLMs is not tested; only 5-layer, width-128 PINNs on 1+1D PDEs are studied.
Not tested: no toy-model geometry, sparsity transition or feature-overlap measurement.
Not tested: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
Not tested: the study uses PINNs, not LLMs. The authors call superposition 'plausible' at this width but do not measure it.
Not tested. Bilateral two-atom codes for signed concepts are an artefact of ReLU non-negativity, not a test of multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Table 8 gives no uncertainty. It does not state how values are aggregated across the 3 PINN seeds. The method section promises a fraction above 0.8, but the table does not report it. There is no chance baseline for Hungarian-matched cosine between random 512-atom dictionaries in 128-d, so 'absent' rests on the low absolute values and the authors' own reading. Rows r1–r24 are four summary statistics of the same measurement per PDE and are not independent. The authors frame instability as expected rather than as a problem.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure feature overlap, decoder-direction geometry, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity as a consequence of capacity limits or compare feature importance and dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Studies PINNs, not LLMs; does not measure LLM feature distribution across neurons or SAE recovery in LLMs.
Tests reproducibility of SAE dictionary atoms across SAE seeds, but not whether SAE features are complete representations or canonical units in a broader sense.
Does not test whether the underlying features superposed in a network are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Six PINN PDE families (Heat, Burgers, Allen–Cahn, Conv. easy, Conv. hard, Schrödinger); D=512 ReLU SAEs, λ=0.02, 3 SAE seeds per PINN
relationships.reason: Matched mean cosine is 0.331–0.371 and median 0.308–0.347. Only 1.1–1.8% of atoms exceed 0.7 and 0.1–0.3% exceed 0.9 (r1–r24). The authors call the dictionaries non-unique. No random-dictionary baseline is given.
relationships.display_finding: Matched atoms had mean cosine 0.331–0.371 and median 0.308–0.347, with only 1.1–1.8% above 0.7 and 0.1–0.3% above 0.9. The authors call the dictionaries non-unique, though no random-dictionary baseline is given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
